claims.claim: LG Washing machine scrap but doesn’t work and needs repair.
claims.evidence: photo 0 shows the machine but provides no proof it is non-working (no power-on test, no error code, no visible damage).

risks.risk: Whether it is truly non-working vs. just not tested (could be a simple issue like power/door latch).
risks.proof: A short video of the machine powered on showing any error code on the display and a failed start attempt (or successful cycle start).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / needs repair (worst case).

risks.risk: Type mismatch: it may be a washer-dryer but the dryer function could be dead even if washing works.
risks.proof: Video showing a wash cycle starting and completing, and then a dryer-only cycle attempt (or dryer error).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as fully non-working for both functions (worst case).

risks.risk: Hidden damage (pump, heater, belt, drum bearings) not visible from the front panel.
risks.proof: Photos of the back panel (power cord area, drain hose connections) and a close-up of the drum interior + any leaks/water stains; plus a technician’s diagnosis note if available.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming major repair may be needed.

risks.risk: Model/age uncertainty affects parts availability and repair cost.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the model/serial rating plate (usually on the door frame or back) so the exact model can be identified.

proof_requests: Send a video: power on + attempt to start, showing any error code/display lights.
Send a video of a wash cycle attempt (even if it fails) and confirm whether water fills and drum spins.
Send a photo of the model/serial plate (rating label) for exact identification.
Send photos of the back panel and drain/power connections to check for damage/leaks.
response.reason: The photo confirms it’s an LG DirectDrive 6/3kg 2-in-1 washer-dryer, but there’s no evidence it doesn’t work. Without a power-on/error or functional test, the worst-case repair pricing can’t be confidently applied.
